scope: Scene-local provider measurements for the current optimizer script. Each scene starts at zero. Unchanged Edge sounds retain their original word triples, boundary hashes and measured durations. Changed beats use the course Kokoro voice. Archived Edge scene hashes and offsets identify the prior edition.

beats.say: Watch both weights take one step. Blue shoots past zero. Green barely moves. They started at one and used the same learning rate. What made blue travel a hundred times as far?

visual_cues.phrase: take one step
Blue shoots past zero
Green barely moves
They started at one and used the same learning rate

beats.say: Back at one, the height of each curve shows its contribution to the loss. The yellow lines show the slopes. Blue has a slope of a hundred. Multiply by the learning rate, point zero one eight, and we subtract one point eight. Green has a slope of one, so we subtract just point zero one eight.

visual_cues.phrase: Multiply by the learning rate, point zero one eight, and we subtract one point eight
Green has a slope of one, so we subtract just point zero one eight

caption_starts: and we subtract one point eight

beats.say: Now move the dots. Only the first crosses zero. The total loss fell, but nearly all the second error is still there. Look at the heights. On the left we pay fifty times a squared. On the right we pay half of b squared. Differentiate each term to get the gradient. The slopes are a hundred times a, and just b. Their rates of change have a ratio of a hundred to one. That is the condition number of this quadratic.

visual_cues.phrase: Now move the dots
Look at the heights. On the left we pay fifty times a squared. On the right we pay half of b squared
Differentiate each term to get the gradient

beats.say: Put both coordinates on one map. At the end of the first step, evaluate the gradient again. The steep slope was a hundred. Here it is minus eighty. Which way will the next step go? Subtracting it sends a back across zero. The slope for b is still positive, so b moves a little closer to zero again. Here we can compute the full gradient. With a random minibatch, stochastic gradient descent uses a noisy estimate.

visual_cues.phrase: Here it is minus eighty
Subtracting it sends a back across zero

beats.say: Follow eight completed updates. The crossings shrink, while the shallow error moves slowly. A smaller rate would calm the steep direction and slow the other one too. We are seeing one global multiplier serve two very different curvatures.

visual_cues.phrase: Follow eight completed updates. The crossings shrink, while the shallow error moves slowly

beats.say: Suppose we raise the rate slightly to help the slow coordinate. Will the steep error settle or grow? Keep the starting point and objective fixed. Make the prediction before we run the second trace.

visual_cues.phrase: Will the steep error settle or grow

beats.say: Run the larger rate through eight completed updates. Each steep-coordinate crossing now grows. Substitute the gradient into the update: the old error is multiplied by negative one point one. Shrinking requires a multiplier whose magnitude is below one. That gives the displayed interval for this quadratic.

visual_cues.phrase: Run the larger rate through eight completed updates. Each steep-coordinate crossing now grows
the old error is multiplied by negative one point one

beats.say: Momentum keeps a signed average of gradients. Most of the old average survives and one tenth of the new gradient enters. Start its buffer at zero. Store the first weighted gradient, then replay four parameter updates using this memory.

visual_cues.phrase: Store the first weighted gradient
then replay four parameter updates using this memory

beats.say: Now the steep error is negative. Its current gradient asks a fresh descent step to return toward zero. Retain the old positive memory, add the new negative contribution, and inspect the sum. The memory remains positive. Subtracting it takes the next update farther left, raising the loss.

visual_cues.phrase: Retain the old positive memory
add the new negative contribution
inspect the sum
Subtracting it takes the next update farther left

beats.say: Continue until the steep buffer turns negative and the parameter starts returning. Meanwhile the small gradients in the second coordinate keep reinforcing the same sign. Each coordinate owns its own buffer. This memory changes both direction and scale, so its learning rate deserves a separate experiment.

visual_cues.phrase: Continue until the steep buffer turns negative and the parameter starts returning

beats.say: Adam combines a signed memory with a memory of squared gradient size. Reset at our original point. Store a weighted gradient in the first buffer. Store a weighted square in the second. Squaring keeps magnitude even when a gradient changes sign.

visual_cues.phrase: Store a weighted gradient in the first buffer
Store a weighted square in the second

beats.say: Both buffers started at zero. The observed gradient has received only part of the total weight. Divide the signed buffer by its observed weight, then correct the squared buffer the same way. On this first update, the corrected estimates recover the gradient and its square.

visual_cues.phrase: Divide the signed buffer by its observed weight
then correct the squared buffer the same way

beats.say: Check that bookkeeping with three zero-rate updates. The parameters stay fixed, so the gradient repeats. The raw buffers fill and the step counter advances. Their corrected estimates keep the same values because we divide by the weight actually assigned to observations. Changing gradients still carry their history and lag.

visual_cues.phrase: Check that bookkeeping with three zero-rate updates. The parameters stay fixed, so the gradient repeats. The raw buffers fill and the step counter advances

beats.say: Reset the buffers for one fresh Adam step. Keep the corrected estimates visible. Which coordinate will receive the larger move at our chosen learning rate? Calculate before we build the denominator.

visual_cues.phrase: Which coordinate will receive the larger move at our chosen learning rate

beats.say: Take the square root of each corrected squared estimate. Divide the signed estimate by that scale. The hundred-to-one gradient difference nearly cancels. Multiply both ratios by the learning rate and take the step. Both errors move by about the same amount. A small epsilon guards each denominator; gradients near that scale receive different normalization.
caption_starts: The hundred-to-one gradient difference nearly cancels
Both errors move by about the same amount

visual_cues.phrase: Take the square root of each corrected squared estimate
Divide the signed estimate by that scale
Multiply both ratios by the learning rate and take the step

beats.say: Return every method to the same starting point and reset its buffers. Give each forty gradient evaluations. The listed learning rates belong to the recipes we are testing. Predict which recipe will reduce the shallow error most, then compare both coordinates and the loss.

visual_cues.phrase: Predict which recipe will reduce the shallow error most

beats.say: Advance each run through the same forty updates, using its own current point for each gradient, then keep the completed paths beside their two remaining coordinate errors. At the shared numeric rate, plain descent finishes below momentum here. Our chosen Adam rate reduces both errors. Tuning and validation determine the useful recipe for a real task.
caption_starts: Our chosen Adam rate reduces both errors

visual_cues.phrase: Advance each run through the same forty updates, using its own current point for each gradient, then keep the completed paths beside their two remaining coordinate errors

beats.say: Reset Adam at one on both coordinates. Watch the stored history for the steep coordinate. The first update uses zero rate. Both dots stay put while moments and the counter still advance. The next four rates ramp to the peak. Now each new rate multiplies the step that the moments give us. The dots have started to move. This sequence of rates is the learning rate schedule.

visual_cues.phrase: The first update uses zero rate
The next four rates ramp to the peak

beats.say: Continue the same run through cosine decay. As the rate falls, it changes each displacement produced by the current moments. At the final zero rate, a residual error remains and parameter movement stops. A schedule chooses when to spend the update budget.

visual_cues.phrase: Continue the same run through cosine decay. As the rate falls, it changes each displacement produced by the current moments

beats.say: Compare the last five updates with constant-rate Adam. These runs share the objective, starting state and update budget; only their schedules differ. The decayed run moves less late, yet finishes with larger loss in this example. Use measured progress and validation to choose the peak, decay and training length.

visual_cues.phrase: Compare the last five updates with constant-rate Adam

beats.say: Weight decay pulls parameters toward zero. AdamW subtracts a fraction of each old weight alongside the adaptive data step. Watch that data move first, then the extra shrink. The two contributions come from different inputs to the update.

visual_cues.phrase: Watch that data move first
then the extra shrink

beats.say: Putting an L2 penalty inside the loss instead adds a parameter term to the gradient. That term enters both Adam buffers. For our positive first gradients, normalization keeps the coupled first move nearly unchanged. AdamW adds its distinct shrink. The displayed calculations specify which rule we used.

visual_cues.phrase: adds a parameter term to the gradient
normalization keeps the coupled first move nearly unchanged

beats.say: Bring back the two errors from the opening. This time a starts at minus one half and b at plus one half. Reset the buffers. Keep the rates on the screen. Which methods will cross zero in the first coordinate after one update?

visual_cues.phrase: Which methods will cross zero in the first coordinate after one update

beats.say: Plain descent subtracts the full scaled gradient. Momentum first stores one tenth of that gradient. Adam corrects and normalizes its two fresh buffers. Build each displacement in that order, carrying the original starting point into every calculation.

visual_cues.phrase: Plain descent subtracts the full scaled gradient
Momentum first stores one tenth of that gradient
Adam corrects and normalizes its two fresh buffers

beats.say: Only plain descent crosses zero here. It subtracts a negative gradient, so it moves right. Momentum moves right too, but its empty buffer took in just a tenth of that first gradient. Adam moves about one learning rate to the right. Knowing the sign told us which way. The buffer and the rate told us how far.

visual_cues.phrase: Knowing the sign told us which way
